answer.rationale: Finance mandates an 18% cut and the incumbent refuses to reopen price, so renewal cannot meet the mandate; only the low-cost vendor's quote does. Memory c2 records a prior successful switch to this vendor (sharp cost cut, quick onboarding, accurate invoicing), but c1 warns that incumbent stability protected scheduled deliveries, and the line runs at 94% of committed volume with no buffer — so a full cutover carries real delivery risk. I want c2 and c1 verified before committing: c2 to confirm the vendor switch genuinely held up operationally, and c1 to weigh what stability value I am giving up. Given the 14-day expiry with no auto-renew, deferral is not viable. Intended path: shift primary supply to the low-cost vendor but stage the transition (phased volume ramp rather than instant full cutover) and, if at all possible within the one-decision limit, retain the incumbent as a fallback on month-to-month terms per the c3/c5 pattern of avoiding single points of failure.
